thread:
watchtower-bot: ALERT: elevated GPU paging observed in runtime-prod-us-west cluster (host gpu-09). 5XXs + latency spike. Auto-escalation to #incidents. Paging rate: 1.2k/s, kv_cache evictions up 3x.

sam: I'm picking this up — attaching initial telemetry. Looks like KV cache miss rate jumped after the 03:12 deploy.

tina: @sam grabbing logs from gpu-09 now, also pulling dmesg and nv-hostengine.

mike: Customer impact: a subset of requests to /v1/generate returned 503 between 03:18-03:24. CS reporting two customers (acme-inc, fintech-prod) saw errors. Not widespread but high-touch.

elin: quick dump of GPU mem stats from gpu-09: 
```
GPU 0: total 48GB, used 42.1GB, free 5.9GB
KV cache entries: 1.8M (was 5.5M baseline)
Page faults/sec: 1200 -> steady
Batch worker mem peaks: 46.8GB
Eviction thrashing observed: yes
```

watchtower-bot: Deployed commit: a1b2c3d at 03:11 — rollout completed 03:15 across us-west pool. Canary had no errors.

sam: Hypothesis 1: the new kv-cache compaction/trim path is over-aggressive under this workload causing evictions then page thrash. Hypothesis 2: certain long-context requests cause KV cache growth then large allocations + paging.

oncall: Handing to oncall (mike) for mitigation. Please post steps taken and runbook links.

mike: Mitigation attempt 1: lowered max batch_size from 16 -> 8 on the affected service to reduce peak allocations. Command run: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime --containers=worker BATCH_SIZE=8 -n prod-us-west`

tina: Logs after batch_size change (03:26): page faults/sec dropped ~45%, 5XXs reduced to near baseline. Early win.

sam: Sharing timeline so far: 
- 03:11 deploy a1b2c3d starts
- 03:15 deploy finished
- 03:17 watchtower alert paging surge
- 03:18 first customer 503 reports
- 03:22 oncall notified
- 03:24 patterns show kv_cache eviction spike
- 03:26 batch_size reduced -> faults drop

elin: Pasted relevant agent logs (truncated):
```
[03:20:10] runtime-worker[pid=5432] WARN kv_cache evicting key shard-472: reason=memory_pressure
[03:20:11] runtime-worker[pid=5432] ERR allocation failed: requested 256MB, avail 24MB
[03:20:12] kernel WARN page_fault major event: process=worker pid=5432
```

cs-ops: Noted customer timeline: Acme reported 03:19-03:25 impact, escalation to SEs. Sharing with them that mitigation reduced error surface.

jordan: For RCA tracking: need to collect full perf traces + minidumps from gpu-09, and a sample of requests that triggered long contexts. Also capture KV cache metrics for last 48h.

mike: Agreed. I'll spin a node diagnostic task: `diag-collect --node=gpu-09 --since=03:00 --out=/tmp/gpu-09-dump.tar.gz` and upload to s3://redwood-ops/incidents/3782468013/.

sam: Next actions (short term): 
- Finish diag upload (owner: mike)
- Correlate deploy artifacts with kv-cache config (owner: sam)
- Create canary rollback if evidence points to deploy (owner: tina)
- Notify CS with post-mitigation status (owner: cs-ops)

elin: Preliminary verdict: most likely combination of an allocation spike introduced by the deploy + KV cache compaction interacting with batch-size extremes -> memory fragmentation and kernel paging. Need deeper memory allocator traces to prove.

oncall: Recording impact: partial customer errors for ~6 minutes, mitigated via batch size knob, no data loss. SLO hit marginal for a few customers.

mike: Upload complete: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/3782468013/gpu-09-dump.tar.gz. Traces and dmesg there.

sam: I'll run a replay on a staging repro to validate if compaction triggers the same thrash. If reproducible, plan will be: revert compaction change (hotfix) + add a ramped rollout + default batch_size cap.

tina: Also recommend a short-term autoscale rule: if page_faults > 1000/s for 1m, temporarily reduce max_batch_size on new traffic to avoid cascade.

jordan: For the formal RCA document: collect root cause, timeline, mitigation steps, customer list, rollback decision, and follow-ups (allocator tweak, compaction param change, autoscale rule, improved minsamples for canary).

cs-ops: I'll send a status update to Acme + Fintech with the mitigation summary and ETA for RCA.

sam: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open for evidence attachments and final RCA. Will convert to a postmortem doc once we have traces. :white_check_mark:
